metadata.title: Meridional ranks of iterated Whitehead doubles
metadata.abstract: We prove that every iterated untwisted Whitehead double of a nontrivial two-bridge knot satisfies the meridional rank conjecture. More precisely, for such a knot $K$ and every $N\geq0$, the augmentation rank, meridional rank, and bridge number of $\operatorname{Wh}^N(K)$ are all $2^{N+1}$. We use microlocal sheaf theory and a doubling construction to produce a lower bound for the meridional rank of the Whitehead double, assuming the peripheral data satisfy suitable conditions. For two-bridge knots, the required curves arise from ideal points detecting nonzero boundary slopes. In contrast, the ordinary group rank of an $N$-fold Whitehead double is at most the rank of the companion group plus $N$. We also give a non-example when the doubling construction does not work -- the first Whitehead double of the square knot has augmentation rank at most 5, whereas its meridional rank and bridge number are 6.
